questions.question: What is the difference between cookies, localStorage, and sessionStorage?
questions.title: Cookies vs localStorage vs sessionStorage — Differences & Use Cases
questions.direct_answer:
What is the difference between cookies, localStorage, and sessionStorage?

**In one line:** name the mechanism, where it applies (the browser pipeline, framework hooks, and user-visible outcomes), and the user-visible outcome.

**Interviewers dig into:** Cookies: sent on every HTTP request (auth), size-limited, accessible server-side, HttpOnly possible; localStorage/sessionStorage: client-only, larger, synchronous API.

**Classic weak answer:** Storing JWT in localStorage without realizing it is exposed to any script (XSS risk); HttpOnly cookie is safer.

**Senior finish:** Map each to an auth storage decision, mention Secure/SameSite/HttpOnly cookie flags, and size limits (~4KB cookie vs ~5-10MB storage).

sections.title: Why this question matters
sections.content:
This question — **Cookies vs localStorage vs sessionStorage — Differences & Use Cases** — shows up constantly in **frontend / fullstack** interviews because it separates candidates who memorized docs from candidates who can **reason about real systems**.

**Restate the prompt:** What is the difference between cookies, localStorage, and sessionStorage?

A gold-level answer does four things in order:

1. **Define** the terms in plain English (what it is / what problem it solves).
2. **Explain the mechanism** (what runs when: browser, bundler, framework, network).
3. **Compare trade-offs** (speed vs correctness vs security vs DX) with **when you would not use** the default.
4. **Ground it in production** — caching, auth, observability, tests, or an incident you handled.

Interviewers are listening for: **Cookies: sent on every HTTP request (auth), size-limited, accessible server-side, HttpOnly possible; localStorage/sessionStorage: client-only, larger, synchronous API**.

The fastest way to lose points is: **Storing JWT in localStorage without realizing it is exposed to any script (XSS risk); HttpOnly cookie is safer**.

If you only add one “senior” layer, make it: **Map each to an auth storage decision, mention Secure/SameSite/HttpOnly cookie flags, and size limits (~4KB cookie vs ~5-10MB storage)**.

sections.title: Deep dive — what to say
sections.content:
### What to explain (middle of the answer)

- **Core mechanics:** Cookies: sent on every HTTP request (auth), size-limited, accessible server-side, HttpOnly possible; localStorage/sessionStorage: client-only, larger, synchronous API
- **Concrete shape:** give a small code or config snippet *only if it clarifies* (5–15 lines max).
- **Interviewer follow-ups:** expect “what breaks in production?”, “how do you debug?”, “what would you measure?” — answer them proactively.

### How to sound senior (without rambling)

- Tie the feature to **user-visible outcomes** (performance, accessibility, security).
- Mention **one failure mode** you have actually seen (race, stale cache, hydration mismatch, flaky test).
- Close with **one decision rule** (“choose X when …; choose Y when …”).

sections.title: Trade-offs & senior signal
sections.content:
### Trade-offs interviewers expect you to name

- **Speed vs safety** (types, runtime checks, validation).
- **DX vs constraints** (framework magic vs explicit wiring).
- **SEO / first paint vs interactivity** (SSR/SSG/CSR choices where relevant).
- **Security vs convenience** (tokens, cookies, localStorage, third-party scripts).

### What “book answer” misses

- **Book answer:** repeats definitions.
- **Strong answer:** names **storing JWT in localStorage without realizing it is exposed to any script (XSS risk); HttpOnly cookie is safer** and what you do instead.

questions.question: When should you use IndexedDB instead of localStorage?
questions.title: IndexedDB vs localStorage — When to Use Each
questions.direct_answer:
When should you use IndexedDB instead of localStorage?

**In one line:** name the mechanism, where it applies (the browser pipeline, framework hooks, and user-visible outcomes), and the user-visible outcome.

**Interviewers dig into:** IndexedDB: large, structured, async, indexed, transactional; localStorage: small, sync, string-only; PWAs and offline apps rely on IndexedDB.

**Classic weak answer:** Using localStorage for large JSON blobs that block the main thread on read/write — IndexedDB is async and won't block.

**Senior finish:** Recommend wrapper libs (idb, Dexie) to make the callback-heavy IndexedDB API usable; mention Cache API for offline assets.

interviewer_intent.common_mistake: Using localStorage for large JSON blobs that block the main thread on read/write — IndexedDB is async and won't block
interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: Recommend wrapper libs (idb, Dexie) to make the callback-heavy IndexedDB API usable; mention Cache API for offline assets
